To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel approach for learning a continuous space in which the diffusion of information can be modeled using a heat diffusion model.
we propose an approach to predict information diffusion that is based on a continuous diffusion process on a continuous representation space.

1) the proposed method learns a mapping of the diffusion process to a latent space in which information diffusion can be efficiently modeled using a heat diffusion kernel; 2) the method can learn the latent space from cascade samples without any additional information; 3) in the projection space the solution to the heat diffusion equation can be written in a closed form; and 4) the method is faster than alternative models for predicting the diffusion process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of predicting information diffusion in social networks and more generally the prediction of diffusion processes.
the problem of learning a mapping of the information diffusion process onto a continuous space, in which the diffusion of information can be modeled using a heat diffusion equation.
learning social network embeddings for the purpose of predicting information diffusion on social media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a promising approach that can be used in a wide range of problems where the diffusion of information on a social network has to be modeled.
the proposed method is able to capture the temporal dynamics of diffusion cascades and that it can be applied to a large range of real world networks.

this paper presents a novel approach for modeling information diffusion on social networks, which has several unique features compared to existing ones, and which performs very well both in terms of quality of predictions and inference speed, and that this approach is a very promising one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new model to predict the diffusion of information in social networks, which is more accurate than existing models and can predict diffusion faster than existing models.
our method can learn the diffusion structure from observed cascades, and can be used to predict the diffusion process of new information in an efficient way.
we are able to predict the diffusion of information on a given graph with an accuracy of 90% and an inference time of 10ms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning the latent space is more efficient for diffusion prediction than learning the diffusion kernel directly.
a diffusion kernel can be learned from the temporal diffusion of a piece of information and that this kernel can be efficiently used to predict the future evolution of the diffusion.
learning the diffusion kernel from cascade samples is a promising approach for modeling the dynamics of diffusion cascades.
